- Overestimate prices when sentiment is low (0.00–0.27) and underperform in rising sentiment (0.36+), especially in early forecast periods.
- Overshoot after sharp upward sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment >0.53) — model tends to overreact and peak too early.
- Underestimate in the first 5–7 days of forecast horizon when sentiment is rising — model lags mean reversion.
- When sentiment is consistently low (0.00–0.18) over 3–5 days, model tends to underestimate and then correct sharply — apply upward bias in later days.
- Avoid overfitting to recent high sentiment — if sentiment peaks then drops, model often overcorrects and forecasts too high.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate the final 5–7 days — apply a 2–3% upward adjustment if sentiment remains above 0.36.
- If sentiment is rising but model forecast is flat or declining, model is underestimating — apply upward bias of 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
